title: Learned CT perfusion patterns correlate with pulmonary hypertension
summary: A Bayesian Gaussian-mixture model separated lung attenuation patterns after neural segmentation in CT scans from 52 patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. A larger normal-attenuation fraction was associated with lower pulmonary vascular resistance and other measured severity indicators. These single-centre correlations do not establish causality, prognosis or replacement of catheter measurements.
organization: Charles University; Motol University Hospital; Brno University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Automated CT measures compared with invasive hemodynamics, clinical biomarkers and radiologist annotations, with multiple-comparison correction.
evidence.unknown: External clinical utility and outcome prediction remain unestablished; a fixed three-component assumption and scanner/artifact effects can alter inferred tissue classes.
evidence.ai_role: A learned mixture model fits patient-specific attenuation distributions while a pretrained neural network delineates lungs and veins for spatial quantification.
